title: Lab meeting: paper deadline
segments: Prof. Chen
The ACL submission deadline is February 15th, so we have about three months. Let's go over where each experiment stands.
Huy
The Vietnamese summarization baseline is done. Our fine-tuned model beats the baseline by 2.1 ROUGE-L points on the VLSP test set.
Prof. Chen
That's a decent gain, but reviewers will ask about human evaluation. ROUGE alone won't convince them.
Huy
I can set up a human eval with three annotators on 200 samples. It would cost about 600 dollars on our annotation budget.
Prof. Chen
Approved. Please keep inter-annotator agreement above 0.6 kappa, otherwise we need to revise the guidelines.
Anna
On the code-switching experiments, I'm blocked. The GPU cluster queue is about four days long right now.
Prof. Chen
I'll ask the department for priority access, we have a deadline argument. In the meantime run the small 1B model locally.
Anna
Okay. I also found that our tokenizer splits Vietnamese syllables badly, about 40 percent more tokens than for English.
Prof. Chen
That's actually an interesting finding. Write it up as a short analysis section, it strengthens the paper.
Huy
Should we also release the dataset?
Prof. Chen
Yes, but check the license of the news sources first. Huy, find out by next Monday whether we can redistribute.
Anna
Who's writing the related work section?
Prof. Chen
Anna drafts related work, Huy drafts experiments. First full draft due January 20th so we have time for internal review.

key_points.point: Fine-tuned model beats baseline by 2.1 ROUGE-L on VLSP
Anna blocked by 4-day GPU queue; ask for priority access, run 1B model locally
Tokenizer uses ~40% more tokens for Vietnamese; write analysis section
Release dataset after checking news source licenses (Huy, by Monday)
